channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Bam Knight (concussion) was not spotted at Thursday’s practice.
item.description: It appears it’ll be another DNP for Knight as he entered the concussion protocol following Sunday’s win over the Cowboys in Week 8. The 25-year-old tailback seems unlikely to be able to go in Week 9 against the Seahawks, but there should be further updates on Knight’s status soon.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: DJ Turner (heel) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description: The Bengals No. 1 cornerback is firmly on track to play in Week 9 against the Falcons. While Drake London would get a matchup boost if Turner were to sit out, Turner’s presence does not drop London out of the WR1 tier.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh indicated that Omarion Hampton will get more touches.
item.description: Harbaugh reportedly made comments to this effect earlier in the week. When asked for his thoughts on the matter, OC Mike McDaniel said he is “excited about someone dictating the rotation” and added that Hampton has “had a really great week of prep.” Hampton hasn’t scored double-digit half-PPR points since Week 4. Whether the potential usage increase can get him back to 10.0-plus points remains to be seen, but this week’s comments are at least somewhat encouraging.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description: Barkley is again on track to play through his injuries on game day. The Eagles’ offensive centerpiece totaled 54 scrimmage yards, one catch and one touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 8 loss to the Commanders. He may have trouble solidifying a spot in the RB1 tier, given the state of the Eagles’ offense, but he remains a high-end RB2 at worst, based on talent and usage.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Bears placed RB Zavier Scott (thumb) on injured reserve
item.description: Scott has not played on offense at all this season, but he has successfully carved out a role on special teams. According to the Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs, the Bears have reason to believe that Scott’s injured reserve stint “will be on the shorter side.”-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Jaylen Wright (quad) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description: Wright is on track to be available for the Dolphins’ Week 9 game against the Lions, although he is mostly functioning as an infrequently used backup rusher while also serving as the team’s top returner. He is a mid-tier bench stash at this time.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Malik Nabers (undisclosed) was seen working off to the side with trainers on Thursday.
item.description: The Giants have limited Nabers’ practice reps from time to time this season. Although he may end up being listed as a non-participant, we are not currently concerned about his Week 9 availability. The Giants’ No. 1 wide receiver is fully dressed in his typical practice attire. An update will be provided when more info is released.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Kyler Murray (hamstring) “will be ‘week-to-week’ now.”
item.description: Murray reportedly experienced soreness in his hamstring following the Vikings’ Week 8 loss to the Lions. Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings’ Week 9 Monday Night Football game against the Bills, and potentially longer. If Wentz plays well, Murray could be relegated to the backup role. Murray does not necessarily need to be stashed on benches in two-quarterback leagues at this time. This situation is not ideal for him.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Carson Wentz will start for the Vikings in Week 9 against the Bills.
item.description: On Monday, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters that Kyler Murray is dealing with a “sore hamstring.” After breaking the news that Wentz will start for the Vikings’ Monday Night Football game, Schefter revealed that Murray is considered “week-to-week.” Unless Wentz flops and Murray’s strained hamstring recovers quickly, Wentz is seemingly in line to start for more than one game. If he plays well enough, he could end up starting for the rest of the season. Wentz’s installation upgrades the fantasy prospects for Vikings pass catchers. Wentz warrants QB2 treatment at this time.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Deshaun Watson (concussion) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Cleveland’s Mary Kay Cabot indicated yesterday that Shedeur Sanders is seemingly slated to start in Week 9 against the Saints. If that ends up being the case, and Sanders can play well enough, it might be possible for him to steal the starting job from Watson this week. Sanders would be QB2-viable against the Saints.-Nic Bodiford
